Elena — thanks for the detailed pass and the spreadsheets, very helpful. Quick responses inline: 

- Uptime commitment: our standard hosted offering uses a 99.95% monthly uptime commitment (we had previously given you a 99.9 figure in the PoC doc; apologies for the mismatch). For enterprise contracts we can set 99.95%.
- Monthly credit structure: we typically use a graduated credit table tied to percentage of monthly uptime missed and cap credits at 50% of the monthly invoice for the given billing period. I'm attaching our standard credit table in the PDF we sent (SLA_Template_v2.pdf).
- Regional latency SLOs: we can include per-region p95 latency SLOs as an optional addendum. There are operational constraints for multi-region guarantees — we usually limit strict SLOs to regions where the customer pins dedicated capacity. Can you indicate whether Northbridge plans to use Dedicated/GPU-reserved capacity in EU?
- Planned maintenance: we allow scheduled maintenance windows up to 8 hours with advance notice; anything beyond that requires a temporary exception signed by an account exec. We can codify a one-off exception process in the SLA.

Proposed next steps: 1) Ben and I will review the redlines and produce a revised markup with our suggested language for the credit table and regional latency addendum; 2) Legal will review; 3) if agreed, we’ll route to DocuSign.

Can you confirm availability for a 30-min sync on Tues 6/9 at 10am PT?

Thanks,

Ben, Mina,

Thanks — a few clarifications from our side after an internal sync: 

- Annual aggregate cap: Northbridge prefers an annual cap of 100% of a single monthly invoice (not 150%). Our rationale: predictable remediation budget and procurement policy.
- Regional latency: Northbridge is not planning to purchase Dedicated EU capacity for launch; they expect Redwood hosted EU region guarantees for the first 12 months. They’re open to an addendum for dedicated capacity later, but need a hosted EU p95 < 200ms guarantee for onboarding.
- Planned maintenance: we need the exception process to allow a single scheduled maintenance exceeding 6 hours per quarter (not per year).

I attached an updated Regional_latency_buckets.xlsx with traffic splits and a sketch of the credit trigger for regional latency misses. Appreciate if you can propose specific wording for: (A) monthly credit mechanics when both uptime and regional latency are missed in the same month, and (B) the allowable scheduled maintenance exception cadence.

Elena

Subject: Final proposed wording & next steps — SLAs and credit mechanics

Elena — thanks for the clear asks. Below is the proposed compromise language that our legal/commercial teams can sign off on. If you’re aligned we’ll drop this into the contract mark and send to DocuSign.

1) Uptime Commitment
- Redwood guarantees 99.95% Monthly Uptime Percentage (MUP) for the Services.

2) Monthly Credit Table (Uptime misses)
- 99.95% — 99.90%: 10% credit of monthly service fees for affected services
- 99.90% — 99.00%: 25% credit of monthly service fees for affected services
- < 99.00%: 50% credit of monthly service fees for affected services
- Maximum credit per billing period: 50% of the monthly invoice for the affected services.

3) Regional Latency SLO (EU hosted region)
- For the initial 12-month onboarding period Redwood guarantees a regional p95 latency of < 200ms for requests served from Redwood’s EU-hosted endpoints.
- If the regional p95 latency target is missed for the month, Northbridge will be eligible for a regional latency credit equal to 15% of the monthly service fees for affected traffic in that region.

4) Combined Failures (uptime + regional latency in same month)
- When both the Monthly Uptime and Regional Latency SLOs are missed in the same billing period, credits will be calculated independently and then subject to the maximum monthly credit cap (50% of the monthly invoice).

5) Aggregate Annual Cap
- Aggregate credits paid in any rolling 12-month period shall not exceed 100% of a single monthly invoice for the affected services.

6) Scheduled Maintenance Exception
- Redwood will give at least 72 hours' notice for scheduled maintenance windows. Each party agrees a maximum of one scheduled maintenance event exceeding six (6) consecutive hours is permitted per calendar quarter without additional approval. Any additional or longer event requires written exception from an account executive.

7) Operational Review and Performance Audit
- As part of onboarding Redwood will perform a one-time performance review (within the first 30 days of go-live) and provide a report. If significant variance from the latency model in Regional_latency_buckets.xlsx is observed, both parties agree to an implementation plan and a timeline to resolve.

Next steps: 
- Laura to incorporate the language above into the contract draft and track redlines.
- Marissa to prepare the DocuSign envelope and include the SLA addendum.
- Ben / Mina to confirm final commercial terms (monthly invoice baseline and affected services list).

If Northbridge agrees to the language above, please confirm by EOD Friday (2026-06-12) and we’ll proceed to DocuSign. If you prefer a short call, I’m available 6/13 9–11am PT.
